body:
Cleanup owed from #193, caused by #197.

During the microbedecoder onboarding I demoted 17 auto-grounded records from `MAPPED` to `UNMAPPED`, recording a `DEMOTED_TO_UNMAPPED` event on each that says the id is "the signature of a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix".

**That reason is false.** All 17 ids are real, non-obsolete ChEBI terms (verified against live OLS4 — see #197). They failed only because the local ChEBI build is stale and the `CHEBI: 300000` ceiling then reclassified the non-resolution.

## What needs undoing

For each of the 17: restore `ontology_mapping` (the id and label are preserved in the `DEMOTED_TO_UNMAPPED` history entry and in the record `identifier`), set `mapping_status` back to `PENDING_REVIEW` so they rejoin the review cohort rather than jumping straight to `MAPPED`, and append a correcting event — the existing one must stay, since curation history is append-only and the erroneous reasoning is part of the record.

Affected: cefazolin, cefepime, cefixime, cefotiam, ertapenem, imipenem, gentamicin, netilmicin, polymyxin B, colistin sulfate, carbomycin, anisomycin, lysostaphin, 1-chlorobutane, 1-chloropropane, 4-nitrophenyl α-D-galactoside, gamma-cyclodextrin.

## Blocked on #197

Restoring them before the adapter/ceiling is fixed just makes `just validate-products` fail again — the gate will re-reject the same 17. Sequence: #197 first, then this.

## Two related corrections

- These 17 are **not "all antibiotics"**, a claim I repeated in #192, #193's commit message and PR body, and a history record. It is 12 of 17 — 1-chlorobutane, 1-chloropropane, 4-nitrophenyl α-D-galactoside and γ-cyclodextrin are not antibiotics, and lysostaphin is a bacteriolytic endopeptidase. Anyone using that summary to prioritise review would mis-batch them.
- The 17 also still carry the rejected CHEBI CURIE as their record `identifier` — the only 17 of 626 records in `unmapped/` not using an `UNMAPPED_NNNN` placeholder. If #197 resolves in favour of the ids being valid, the identifiers are correct as-is and nothing further is needed; if not, they need re-minting.

A corrected manifest marking these 17 `DEMOTED_IN_ERROR_RESTORE` with the OLS evidence exists but is not committed — #194 still carries the superseded `SUSPECT_ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` labelling.
title: Restore the 17 microbedecoder records I demoted on a false positive

body:
`conf/id_label_targets.yaml` sets `max_accession: CHEBI: 300000`. The validator treats an id that **does not resolve locally AND sits above the ceiling** as "a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix".

During the microbedecoder onboarding (#193) that rule rejected 17 groundings as `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE`, and I acted on it — demoting all 17 to `UNMAPPED`. **That was wrong.**

## Verified against live OLS4

All 17 are **real, non-obsolete ChEBI terms with exactly the labels claimed**:

| id | label |
|---|---|
| `CHEBI:474053` | cefazolin |
| `CHEBI:759883` | colistin sulfate |
| `CHEBI:747005` | 1-chlorobutane |
| `CHEBI:495056` | gamma-cyclodextrin |
| …and 13 more | cefepime, cefixime, cefotiam, ertapenem, imipenem, gentamicin, netilmicin, polymyxin B, carbomycin, anisomycin, lysostaphin, 1-chloropropane, 4-nitrophenyl α-D-galactoside |

They fail only because the **local ChEBI sqlite build is stale** and cannot resolve them, and the ceiling then reclassifies the non-resolution as "foreign identifier".

## The heuristic is not worthless

Checked the same way, #170's `CHEBI:867561` (Sodium L-lactate's identifier) returns **NOT FOUND** from OLS4 — genuinely bogus, correctly caught. So the rule catches real problems; it just cannot distinguish "invalid id" from "valid id my local ontology copy predates".

## Why this matters beyond 17 records

ChEBI keeps minting accessions above 300000. As-is, this gate will reject **every future grounding to a recent ChEBI term**, and the failure presents as "foreign identifier" — which invites exactly the destructive response I took.

## Options

1. **Refresh the local ChEBI adapter** — addresses the root cause; the ceiling then only fires on ids that genuinely don't exist anywhere.
2. **Fall back to OLS4 before declaring ID_OUT_OF_RANGE** — a non-resolving id above the ceiling gets one live lookup before being called foreign. Slower, but it is the check that would have prevented this.
3. Raise the ceiling — cheapest, but it weakens the one signal that correctly caught #170.

(1) or (2). Related: #170, #193, #195.
title: The CHEBI accession ceiling mis-rejects valid recent terms — 17 false positives, verified against live OLS4

body:
Found while grounding the microbedecoder UNMAPPED residual (the free normalized/fuzzy pass on `feat/microbedecoder-residual-grounding`).

The #193 import demoted 17 auto-groundings to `UNMAPPED` as "SUSPECT_ID_OUT_OF_RANGE" — CHEBI ids above the `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` `max_accession: CHEBI: 300000` ceiling. On inspection, **11 of the 17 are valid, current CHEBI terms that resolve in the local `chebi.db`** and were demoted purely for their accession number:

`CHEBI:338412` (-)-anisomycin · `CHEBI:474053` cefazolin · `CHEBI:478164` cefepime · `CHEBI:472657` cefixime · `CHEBI:355510` cefotiam · `CHEBI:404903` ertapenem · `CHEBI:471744` imipenem · `CHEBI:495056` gamma-cyclodextrin · `CHEBI:747004/747005` 1-chloropropane/1-chlorobutane · `CHEBI:546840` 4-nitrophenyl alpha-D-galactoside

## Root cause

Two different range rules disagree:

- **The id↔label gate** (`scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py`) only returns `ID_OUT_OF_RANGE` when the id **does not resolve** AND is above the ceiling (the ceiling is a tie-breaker for *unresolvable* ids — "a PubChem CID wearing a CHEBI prefix"). A locally-resolving above-ceiling id passes as `OK_CANONICAL`. Correct.
- **The import's demotion logic** applied the ceiling as a *hard cap* regardless of resolution, so it demoted resolvable terms the gate would have accepted.

The local `chebi.db` reaches accession **747618**; modern CHEBI legitimately issues ids far above 300000. The ceiling number cannot by itself distinguish a real `CHEBI:759086` from a foreign CID — resolution is the real test, which is exactly what the gate already does.

## Done in the grounding branch
Re-promoted the 11 to MAPPED (all `EXACT_MATCH`, id↔label gate green). No config change was needed because the gate already accepts them.

## Suggested fix (import path)
Align the importer's demotion with the gate: demote on **(above ceiling AND unresolvable)**, not on the ceiling alone. Otherwise every future import re-demotes valid high-accession CHEBI terms.

## Still genuinely blocked (separate, not fixed here)
6 ids exceed local coverage (>747618) — valid & current in OLS but absent from the local `chebi.db`, so they cannot pass the local gate until the db is refreshed: `CHEBI:756054` carbomycin · `CHEBI:759883` colistin sulfate · `CHEBI:759884` gentamicin · `CHEBI:753395` lysostaphin · `CHEBI:748901` netilmicin · `CHEBI:759086` polymyxin B. Triage TSV: `mappings/microbedecoder_demoted_antibiotics_triage.tsv`. These stay demoted pending a `chebi.db` refresh (or an OLS fallback in the gate).
title: microbedecoder import over-demoted 11 valid CHEBI antibiotics via a stale 300000 accession ceiling
